clue.text: A Page 3 star?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a glamour model from the Sun newspaper's notorious page 3, admired for her figure
cryptic reading: a star in the sky is a celestial object

explanation.surface: A tabloid pin-up girl being described.
explanation.walkthrough: Page 3 of the British Sun newspaper famously carried photos of topless models; such a model might be said to have a divine figure, while a star is also an astronomical object.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars and planets are celestial objects, and the phrase also means a gorgeous figure.

clue.text: Employees take standing order to a cashier!

parts.note: hands are workers, as in farm hands
up as in on your feet, not sitting

explanation.surface: Staff set up a regular bank payment with a teller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing order' looks like a bank instruction, but the order is the one a robber barks at the cashier.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the command a bank robber gives a teller to raise both arms in surrender.

clue.text: Dec's co-star's elevation at workers' home

parts.note: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo, so Dec's partner is Ant
a hill is a raised piece of ground

explanation.surface: A TV presenter's hilltop residence near his staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a famous British television double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants live in the mound their colony builds.

clue.text: Damned flower put in a box

parts.note: a river is something that flows; the Exe is a river in Devon
crated means packed into a crate

explanation.surface: A cursed bloom packaged up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword code for a river, here the Exe in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or denounce, so the past form means cursed.

clue.text: Bishop's see previously next to large hall

indicators.note: comes before, so the word for see goes ahead of the bishop

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
B is the chess notation for bishop
by meaning beside

explanation.surface: A cathedral diocese sits beside a big hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a bishop's diocese, but it is the exclamation lo.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance hall or foyer of a large building, such as the one in Parliament.

clue.text: Surprised call of "Roger, out" in British Airways

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the airline's initials
out as in out of order, so the letters of roger are scrambled

parts.note: the radio word is used as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pilot's radio message on a BA flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger, out' is radio-speak, but out signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish exclamation of surprise, a softened form of 'by God'.

clue.text: Power supply means TT race half completed by learners

indicators.note: the learners come at the end

parts.note: teetotal, so not drinking

indicators.note: only half of the word race is used, its second half

parts.note: the word itself, of which only its back half is kept
two L-plates, L being the learner driver abbreviation

explanation.surface: The Isle of Man TT motorbike race being finished by novice riders.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is a famous Isle of Man motorcycle race, but here TT means teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery cell with a paste electrolyte, used to provide electrical energy.

clue.text: A Law Lords' fad curiously unknown to Basil Fawlty?

indicators.note: oddly, in a strange arrangement, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: these words supply exactly the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A legal fashion among the senior judges that a TV hotelier had never heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Fawlty Towers episode, hotelier Basil Fawlty (John Cleese) is flustered when a guest orders a dish he has never heard of; the Law Lords were Britain's highest judges.
explanation.definitionFit: The celery, apple and walnut dish that Basil's kitchen could not make in the sitcom.

clue.text: Trap (stakeout) gets the bird!

indicators.note: the stake sits outside the trap

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake
a net catches things

explanation.surface: A police stakeout traps a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stakeout' splits into stake and out. 'Bird' is British slang for a girl or woman, so a girl's name fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, and bird is informal British slang for a young woman.

clue.text: Mike, out of sight, watched with astonishment

parts.note: a hidden microphone is a bug
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: Someone stared in amazement at a man named Mike disappearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike looks like a man's name but it is a microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Having eyes popping out, as a person staring in amazement does.

clue.text: Underworld burial gets exposure

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and his realm
interment is putting a body in a grave

explanation.surface: A funeral in Hades attracts publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word, though 'burial' tempts as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Digging up a buried body brings it to light, figuratively revealing what was hidden.

clue.text: Tramp about, single file

indicators.note: around, so the tramp surrounds the single

parts.note: a dosser is a homeless person sleeping rough
one, written as the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A vagrant shuffles around in a line on his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single file' reads as a queue, but file is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of documents about a person or subject.

clue.text: Deliveries to the Orkneys — no name but right otherwise

indicators.note: in another way, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the name is removed from the islands' word

parts.note: the Scottish islands' name, used for its letters
R

explanation.surface: Parcels being sent to the Scottish isles.
explanation.walkthrough: A yorker is a cricket ball bowled to land at the batsman's feet; 'deliveries' is the cricket sense, not post.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket each ball bowled is a delivery, and these are a particular kind of ball.

clue.text: Be disgusting, quietly breaking wind

indicators.note: splitting the word apart to sit inside it

parts.note: to reel in is to wind a line

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly passing gas is being revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking wind' suggests a fart; wind here is the verb to wind, as a fishing reel does.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to revolt or cause aversion in someone.

clue.text: Waterproof cracked urinal tap

indicators.note: broken apart, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: these two words supply the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A broken fitting in a gents' lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarred or plastic sheet used to keep rain off things.

clue.text: See poplar shaped as a fruit tree

indicators.note: formed into a new arrangement, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: these two words supply the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gardener points at a poplar pruned to look like an orchard tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical tree of the myrtle family bearing rose-scented edible fruit.

clue.text: Red seen as odd for evening performances

indicators.note: strange, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: these three words supply the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A strange colour spotted at a night-time show.
explanation.definitionFit: Songs sung at night beneath a lover's window are the classic example.

clue.text: One making amends for revolution against one's queen

indicators.note: next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: rev, a single turn of an engine
one is, I plus is
Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A rebel making peace after rising against the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amends' here means amendments, not reparations.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who corrects or edits a text is changing it for the better.

clue.text: Part of river where alternative king's involved in swan-upping

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the result is turned backwards
placed inside the bird's name

parts.note: the bird's name, used for its letters
or, as in this or that
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A different monarch taking part in the annual Thames swan count.
explanation.walkthrough: Swan-upping is the yearly census of the swans on the River Thames, which belong to the Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow stretch of a river or strait where the channel tightens.

clue.text: Follow directions and take action

parts.note: east and north, two compass points
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Obey the instructions and act on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow directions' reads as one instruction; follow is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To result or come after something as a consequence.

clue.text: Emanates from old Henry's quarters

parts.note: ex as in former
Hal, the nickname of Prince Henry in Shakespeare
east and south, two of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: Something wafts out of an ancient king's lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' suggests living rooms but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe out or give off, as vapour or air, is to emit.

clue.text: Spurs' top player could be the oldest in town?

definitions.text: could be the oldest in town?

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the club's name supplies only its first letter
a winger plays on the wing in football

explanation.surface: Tottenham's leading footballer might be the club veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur football club. The definition plays on the phrase 'the oldest swinger in town'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively, fashionable person, as in the jokey phrase about an ageing party-goer.

clue.text: Bar alien with little hair, say

definitions.note: a young hare, with hair standing in for its sound-alike

parts.note: a lever is a rigid bar used to prise
ET, the film extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A space creature is refused entry because of a meagre hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition depends on hair sounding like hare.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hare in its first year is the term for the baby animal.

clue.text: Bore child, small boy

parts.note: a tot is a small child
Ed, a shortened boy's name

explanation.surface: A woman gave birth to a little son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore child' suggests giving birth; bore is carried.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry, so the past tense means carried.

clue.text: One article is first of many on godlessness

parts.note: a as in one
the definite article
taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the word supplies only its opening letter

explanation.surface: A single essay is the lead piece of many on unbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbelief in the existence of any deity.

clue.text: Dole receiver's dismissed

parts.note: a satellite dish receives signals
out, as a batsman is in cricket

explanation.surface: A benefits claimant has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dole' suggests unemployment benefit, but here it is the verb to hand out.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute in portions, as one does when handing out food or money.

clue.text: "Parrot is no more!", announced in sketch with many lines?

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: Polly is the stock parrot's name, and gone means dead

explanation.surface: A reference to Monty Python's dead parrot sketch, famous for its many lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The parrot in Monty Python's dead parrot sketch 'is no more'; 'sketch' here is a drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane figure bounded by many straight sides, which can be drawn as a sketch.

clue.text: Eddie Izzard is very unhappy with theatre assistant?

definitions.note: a British comedian well known for performing in women's clothes

parts.note: cross as in angry
a dresser helps actors with costumes

explanation.surface: A comedian is upset with a backstage helper.
explanation.walkthrough: Eddie Izzard is a British comedian who has long performed in dresses and make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedian is a famous example of someone wearing clothes associated with the other sex.
